headline: Equity-market gains power a record quarter
summary_short: RLI's second-quarter net income rose 35.2% y/y to $168 million ($1.82 diluted EPS) on $103 million of unrealized equity-portfolio gains and a 30th-consecutive-year underwriting profit of $60 million on an 85.6 combined ratio, while gross premiums written grew on continued casualty-segment strength.
summary_long: Second-quarter net income rose 35% y/y to $168 million ($1.82 diluted EPS), driven mainly by $103 million of unrealized equity-portfolio gains (versus $43.5 million a year ago) and continued underwriting profit -- $60 million on an 85.6 combined ratio, aided by $40 million of favorable prior-year reserve releases that offset a higher 40.1 expense ratio from workforce investment. Net investment income rose 17% to $46 million on higher reinvestment rates. RLI issued $300 million of 5.375% senior notes in March, lifting debt to $297 million, paid a $2.00 special dividend, launched a $250 million buyback, and raised its regular dividend 12.5% to $0.18/share. Shareholders' equity fell 2.5% q/q to $1,752 million on the dividend outflow.

drivers.explanation: The $15 million increase was driven by continued growth within the casualty segment on favorable rate movement and expanding personal-umbrella distribution.
Growth reflects premium growth plus net investment income up 17% and a $60 million favorable swing in net unrealized equity-securities gains versus a year ago.
Growth driven by higher underwriting income, 17% growth in net investment income, and a $103 million net unrealized equity-securities gain versus $43.5 million a year ago.
Tracked the net-income gain; diluted share count was roughly flat y/y (92.16M vs 92.52M).

Expense ratio rose to 40.1 from 38.6 on continued workforce investment and higher acquisition costs, partly offset by a lower 45.5 loss ratio from greater favorable reserve development and lower catastrophe losses.
Increase was due to higher reinvestment rates and an increased average asset base relative to the prior year.
Fell q/q as the $184 million special dividend paid in June plus $12 million of share buybacks outweighed operating cash generation.
Debt roughly tripled y/y after RLI issued $300 million of 5.375% senior notes due 2036 in March 2026, netting $297 million after discounts and costs.
Fell q/q as the $184 million special dividend and $12 million of buybacks outweighed the quarter's net income and a small other-comprehensive-loss.
30th consecutive year of underwriting profitability; growth was broad-based across segments though casualty and surety combined ratios each rose y/y while property's improved.
